explanation: The monk Dionysius Exiguus devised AD numbering in 525 for his Easter tables. Caliph Umar adopted the Hijri calendar around 638, counting from Muhammad's move to Medina in 622.

claims.text: Dionysius Exiguus introduced the AD (Anno Domini) system of numbering years in AD 525, in his tables for calculating Easter.
The Hijri calendar, which counts years from the Hijra, was adopted under Caliph Umar around AD 638.
The Hijra, Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina, took place in AD 622.
